source.title: The Effect of Berberine on Metabolic Profiles in Type 2 Diabetic Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
source.source_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials

extraction_metadata.scope_note: This is a secondary systematic review. Meta-analysis findings are atoms for the review's own synthesis and are tagged as secondary-source evidence. Bibliographic entries and study-level findings from cited trials were not converted into primary-study atoms. All model-extracted atoms remain needs_review pending independent human verification.

atoms.canonical_statement: The review evaluated the efficacy and safety of berberine for patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we conducted this systematic review and meta-analysis to examine the efficacy and safety of berberine in the treatment of patients with type 2 DM.

atoms.canonical_statement: The review was registered in PROSPERO as CRD42020155086 and reported use of Cochrane and PRISMA methods.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: performed according to the Cochrane Handbook ... reported according to Preferred Reporting Items ... The protocol has been registered on PROSPERO as CRD42020155086.

atoms.canonical_statement: The search covered PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, SinoMed, Wanfang, and Chinese VIP Information through March or April 2021 without language or date restrictions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The literature research was conducted with the use of the following eight databases with no time restriction

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials with at least 60 participants and at least 4 weeks of intervention.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: only RCTs were eligible ... sample size was greater than or equal to 60 participants, and the intervention duration was no less than four weeks

population.label: Eligible randomized trials with at least 60 participants and at least 4 weeks of intervention

atoms.canonical_statement: Two investigators independently screened titles and abstracts, and two authors independently extracted data using standard forms.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Titles and abstracts were screened independently by two investigators ... Data extraction was carried out independently by two authors using standard data extraction forms

atoms.canonical_statement: Two reviewers independently assessed risk of bias with the Cochrane risk of bias tool, with a third reviewer resolving disagreements.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Two reviewers independently assessed the quality of each article, using the risk of bias assessment tool in the Cochrane. Another reviewer was asked to help decide if there was a disagreement.

atoms.canonical_statement: Categorical outcomes were pooled as risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals, while continuous outcomes used mean differences or standardized mean differences.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Categorical outcomes were expressed as risk ratio (RR) with 95% confident intervals (CI), while continuous measurement was pooled by the standardized mean difference (SMD) or mean difference (MD).

atoms.canonical_statement: The review defined I-squared values above 50% with P below 0.1 as significant heterogeneity and used random-effects models when heterogeneity was observed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: when I2 was greater than 50% and P < 0.1, the heterogeneity among the trials was significant ... A random effects model was applied if there was any heterogeneity observed.

atoms.canonical_statement: The review planned subgroup analyses for treatment method, sensitivity analyses with leave-one-out removal for high heterogeneity, and funnel plots for publication bias.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Subgroup analysis was planned ... Sensitivity analyses were conducted using a leave-one-out method ... Funnel plots were planned to assess publication bias

atoms.canonical_statement: Supplementary File 1 contains the full PubMed search history used for the review.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Supplementary Files 1 shows the full electronic search strategy for PubMed according to the search history.

atoms.canonical_statement: The quantitative synthesis included 46 clinical trials published from 2004 through 2021.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A total of 46 clinical trials were considered and included in the quantitative meta-analysis ... publication time ... from 2004 to 2021.

atoms.canonical_statement: Across included trials, 4,158 participants were enrolled, with 2,063 in experimental groups and 2,095 in control groups.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A total of 4,158 participants were enrolled, including 2,063 participants in the experimental group and 2,095 participants in the control group.

atoms.canonical_statement: Twenty-two included trials reported random sequence generation, five reported allocation concealment and blinded outcome assessment, and five reported blinding of participants and personnel.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: twenty-two of them provided information on random sequence generation. Five studies reported information on allocation concealment procedures and the blindness of outcome assessments. Five studies were conducted with blinding of both participants and personnel.

atoms.canonical_statement: Most included trials were conducted in Chinese patients, limiting generalizability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: most of the trials were conducted among Chinese patients, which limited the widespread application of this data.

atoms.canonical_statement: Substantial statistical heterogeneity affected several comparisons, and the review could not identify a single primary source.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: excessive statistical heterogeneity appeared in some comparisons; however, the primary source of heterogeneity could not be determined.

atoms.canonical_statement: The quality of included trials was uneven, and many did not report blinding or allocation concealment methods.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: literature qualities were uneven ... Many of these studies did not report the methods of blinding and allocation concealment.

atoms.canonical_statement: The review lacked enough long-term berberine data to assess diabetic complication risk.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: more information on the long-term intervention of berberine ... is needed to assess the occurrence risk of diabetic complications.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that berberine improved glucose and lipid metabolism, insulin resistance, and inflammation in patients with type 2 diabetes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: berberine positively regulated glucose metabolism and lipids, improving insulin resistance and inflammation in patients with T2DM.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors recommended berberine as adjunctive therapy for type 2 diabetes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Thus, berberine was recommended as an adjunctive therapy for T2DM.
